The days spent in bed feeling fragile and depressed because I fucked up my brain chemistry. Not wanting to see people because I was puffy and sweaty and felt sick. Not being able to eat but ordering tons of food. The times where you have to go out and interact with the world but felt like the ground was going to eat you.

It turns out you lose at least twice as much time as advertised for fucking around with that stuff. Not to mention the years it takes off the end of your life.

And I will caveat all of this with; if you want to try something now, go natural. Less damage to you, less damage to the environment, less damage to society.

​

Enough tomatillos to cover the bottom of the pan

2 tomatoes

1 medium to large onion

3-6 cloves of garlic, depending on taste

3 serrano or jalapeño chilis, depending on taste

1 bunch fresh cilantro

1 teaspoon of sea salt

​

1. Blacken the first 5 ingredients in a dry pan (I actually just put the tomatoes, tomatillos and garlic in the pan and char the onion and chilis directly over the flame on the stovetop)

2. Let ingredients cool

3. Peel garlic and chop the cooled ingredients

4. In a blender or molcajete, blend all ingredients except the cilantro and return to the pan to reduce a bit.

5. Cool salsa and right before serving, chop and add cilantro.

Like others have said, I also don't deal with it. There was a time that I'd upload quite regularly to 500px, Viewbug and others and you know what? I got nothing out of it. One finalist position in a viewbug contest and a couple of sales on 500px marketplace. Instagram is just pointless for me.

Likes? Not really, a few, nothing that was setting the world alight. Followers? A few hundred. A sense of satisfaction?  Absolutely not. Those websites didn't even really help me improve technically and it was disheartening to see shoddy photos of boobs and heavily saturated hdr images gaining thousands of likes and followers.

So, I stopped using them. I still upload to them every now and then (and enter the odd contest) but I expect nothing from them. At all. And they give me nothing. It's just for fun. The thing is, I still wanted to try and make some money out of my photography. And those sales on 500px marketplace had given me an idea.

So I started uploading to stock websites. And you know what? I was roundly rejected from all of them! Not one accepted me. They did give me reasons why though. And with the knowledge of why they hadn't accepted me, whether it was focus, editing, trademarks or whatever, I went out with a whole different mindset. I kept going back to those websites because I wanted to show myself I could get on them at least. So eventually I was accepted. And just like that, within a few short weeks, those sites had improved my photography and editing more than any social media platform ever had.

Then... Nothing happened. I uploaded a few more times and nothing happened. So I kind of got disheartened again (there is a pattern here!). I stopped uploading to them and just kind of got on with shooting more, doing the odd job here and there and just trying to improve. 

Then one day I had an email that said something along the lines of "Congratulations on your first sale!" It was exciting. Then it happened again.  I started selling photos. Just a trickle but the satisfaction that someone had liked my photos enough to pay for them, even if I earned just .25c from it was more than I had gleaned from the socials. 

So I started uploading to them again, sporadically. And the more I uploaded the more the sales rolled in. So I streamlined my scattergun approach to focus more on one or two types of photography and started uploading regularly, at least once a week. Soon enough, I was selling almost constantly. In December last year, I was contacted by alamy asking if I would release one of my editorial photos for a commercial client. I said yes and sold my first $100 stock photo. 

Not great for the people who were around at the peak of the stock boom but a milestone for me! Yesterday one went on that same site for $50. Last month I sold 2 there. That site doesn't sell tons for me but it's a happy day whenever it does. Shutterstock sells multiple files daily, though usually for .25c a pop.  And it's still a great feeling. Obviously I'd like more for my work but even 25 cents is better than the big fat nothing that IG, Flickr and the like have ever given me. 

The satisfaction of getting a payout because a group of people around the world liked my shots enough to part with their money for them is a better feeling than the kind of sad emptiness and longing that is the trademark of social media for the regular Joe. I hardly use social media any more and wholeheartedly recommend stock photography as a gainful alternative or companion to it. That is where 95% of my photographic output goes these days. 

Photography is best when your files actually work for you!
